components: AsyncWebCrawler (the core async crawler; used as `async with AsyncWebCrawler() as crawler`)
AdaptiveCrawler (scores page relevance to a query and stops when confident it has enough)
Markdown generators: DefaultMarkdownGenerator (produces result.markdown and result.markdown.fit_markdown)
architecture_facts: Turns raw web pages into clean, LLM-ready Markdown (result.markdown) with an optional filtered fit_markdown for RAG
The AdaptiveCrawler scores each page's relevance to the query and keeps a running confidence, exploring only relevant content instead of the whole site
Deep crawl supports BFS, DFS, and Best-First traversal so exploration order is a first-class choice, not fixed
Secure-by-default Docker deployment with browser control; runs fully local, no API key required for the crawl itself
Content filtering (Pruning / BM25) strips boilerplate before markdown so only signal survives
surprising_detail: The Adaptive Crawler does not crawl a whole site — it measures its own confidence that it has learned enough about your query and STOPS mid-site once it crosses that threshold, exploring only relevant pages instead of spidering everything.
